title: warpVector
body:
## warpVector

Moves every point by scale times a three-component point vector (new position = point + scale x vector), typically to show a structural displacement field or exaggerate a deformation mode. The output keeps the input type (image data and rectilinear grids become structured grids) and carries all arrays. With scale 1 and a displacement in the same length units as the coordinates the result is the true deformed shape; warping by a velocity is only a visual distortion.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The displacement must be in the coordinate units: a displacement in millimetres on a mesh in metres needs scale 0.001 for the true shape.
- Large scales can fold or invert cells; do not compute volumes or mesh quality on an exaggerated warp.
- Schemaxis's serial native acceptance run (examples/schemaxis/extended-coverage.json) executes this operation once, on a wavelet with a uniform vector field and scale 0.25; it does not check this operation's output values, so inspect the result on your own data.

Native constructor: `WarpByVector`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet); image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet","vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vectors` | Two entries naming the displacement vectors: the association token POINTS and the name of a three-component point array, e.g. ["POINTS", "displacement"]. Each point moves by scale times its vector. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `scale` | Each component of the selected vector array will be multiplied by the value of this property before being used to compute new point coordinates. | `{"type":"number"}` | `1` | `1` |

Cross-option checks:

```json
[
  {
    "kind": "firstItem",
    "option": "vectors",
    "values": [
      "POINTS"
    ],
    "code": "INVALID_ASSOCIATION",
    "message": "warpVector reads the selected array per point; the CELLS association is not supported",
    "recovery": "name a POINTS array; convert cell data first with cellToPoint"
  }
]
```

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "warpVector",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  },
  "options": {
    "vectors": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE",
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
